default_must_not_infer: honesty or integrity from a single inconsistency
competence from accent, grammar or fluency
culture fit from manner or style

competencies.name: Communication & articulation
competencies.definition: Makes points clearly, in a sensible order, at the right level of detail for the listener, and answers the question asked.
strong: leads with the answer then supports it
red: repeatedly does not answer the question asked
competencies.structure: Point first, then support, then close.

competencies.name: Structured thinking
competencies.definition: Breaks problems and answers into clear, non-overlapping parts and moves through them deliberately.
strong: states a structure before diving in
parts do not overlap and cover the space
red: forces a memorised framework that does not fit the problem

competencies.name: Problem solving
competencies.definition: Diagnoses root causes, generates and tests options, and reaches a workable solution under constraints.

competencies.name: Analytical reasoning
competencies.definition: Draws sound conclusions from data and evidence, and knows what the data can and cannot show.
strong: states what the data implies and its limits

competencies.name: Quantitative reasoning
competencies.definition: Handles numbers accurately and uses them to support decisions.
red: fundamental unit or magnitude errors that change the conclusion

competencies.name: Commercial & business judgment
competencies.definition: Connects decisions to customers, revenue, cost, risk and competitive position, and makes sensible trade-offs.
red: recommendation that clearly destroys value without acknowledging it

competencies.name: Ownership & accountability
competencies.definition: Takes responsibility for outcomes, is clear about personal contribution, and follows through.
strong: distinguishes own actions from the team's
owns a mistake and the fix
competencies.structure: Situation -> my responsibility -> my actions -> result -> learning.

competencies.name: Leadership
competencies.definition: Sets direction, mobilises people without relying only on authority, develops others and makes hard calls.
strong: explains a hard call and its trade-off
red: team-size or scope claims that do not hold up
competencies.structure: Context -> what I did to lead -> how people responded -> outcome -> learning.

competencies.name: Stakeholder management
competencies.definition: Understands what different stakeholders need and secures alignment and buy-in.
competencies.structure: Stakeholders and their interests -> approach -> outcome.

competencies.name: Collaboration & teamwork
competencies.definition: Works effectively with others, shares credit and information, and helps the team succeed.

competencies.name: Conflict management
competencies.definition: Addresses disagreements directly and constructively and moves to a resolution.
strong: states the other party's view fairly
weak: frames the other person as simply wrong

competencies.name: Situational judgment
competencies.definition: Chooses sensible, ethical and practical actions in realistic job situations with incomplete information.
strong: chooses a defensible action and says why
red: proposes clearly unethical or unsafe action
competencies.structure: Clarify -> options -> choose -> why -> what I'd watch.

competencies.name: Prioritisation & execution
competencies.definition: Decides what matters most with limited time and resources and gets it done.
strong: names what they would drop and why

competencies.name: Self-awareness & learning
competencies.definition: Reflects honestly on what worked and what did not, and changes behaviour as a result.
strong: shows a later example of applying it
weak: failure that is really a humble-brag
competencies.structure: What happened -> my part -> lesson -> how I applied it since.

competencies.name: Motivation & role understanding
competencies.definition: Has a credible, specific reason for wanting this role and understands what it involves day to day.
strong: links past choices to this role coherently
describes real day-to-day of the role
competencies.structure: Past -> why this -> why now -> what I bring.

competencies.name: Company & industry understanding
competencies.definition: Understands the company's business, market and the role's contribution to it.
strong: accurate, specific understanding of how the business makes money
competencies.structure: Business -> market -> implication for the role.

competencies.name: Handling challenge & pushback
competencies.definition: Defends reasoning with evidence when challenged and updates position when shown to be wrong. Assessed only on observable responses to pushback.
strong: responds to pushback with evidence or a reasoned concession
weak: repeats the same point without new support

competencies.name: Functional knowledge
competencies.definition: Depth of knowledge in the role's function, applied correctly to realistic situations.
strong: explains concepts correctly and applies them

competencies.name: Technical depth
competencies.definition: Depth and correctness of technical knowledge needed for the role.

competencies.name: Financial statement analysis
competencies.definition: Reads and connects the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, and interprets ratios.
strong: traces an item across all three statements
explains what a ratio change implies

competencies.name: Valuation
competencies.definition: Values businesses and assets with DCF, multiples and other methods and knows their limits.
strong: chooses method for the situation and explains why
red: internally inconsistent cash flow and discount rate

competencies.name: Corporate finance
competencies.definition: Capital structure, cost of capital, capital budgeting, working capital and funding decisions.
strong: reasons about trade-offs between funding options

competencies.name: Financial modelling
competencies.definition: Builds and reviews models that are structured, driver-based and checkable.

competencies.name: Financial markets & instruments
competencies.definition: Understanding of equities, fixed income, derivatives and how markets price risk.
strong: explains payoffs and pricing drivers correctly

competencies.name: Risk management
competencies.definition: Identifies, measures and mitigates credit, market, operational or project risk.

competencies.name: Credit analysis
competencies.definition: Assesses a borrower's ability and willingness to repay.

competencies.name: Accounting & audit
competencies.definition: Applies accounting standards and audit procedures correctly.

competencies.name: FP&A & budgeting
competencies.definition: Plans, forecasts and explains variances to support business decisions.

competencies.name: Consumer insight
competencies.definition: Understands consumer needs, behaviour and decision journeys and turns them into actionable insight.
strong: distinguishes an insight from an observation

competencies.name: Brand management
competencies.definition: Builds and manages brand positioning, equity and the marketing mix.

competencies.name: Pricing
competencies.definition: Sets and changes prices using value, cost and competition, and anticipates reactions.

competencies.name: Go-to-market & channels
competencies.definition: Plans how a product reaches and wins customers: segments, channels, distribution and launch.
strong: channel choice tied to customer and economics
competencies.structure: Who -> how they buy -> channel -> economics -> plan.

competencies.name: Digital & performance marketing
competencies.definition: Runs measurable acquisition and engagement across digital channels.

competencies.name: Market research
competencies.definition: Designs research that answers business questions and interprets it honestly.

competencies.name: Category & trade management
competencies.definition: Manages a category's assortment, pricing, promotion and retailer relationships for growth.

competencies.name: Marketing metrics & analytics
competencies.definition: Defines, measures and interprets marketing performance.
strong: chooses the right metric and baseline

competencies.name: Growth & retention
competencies.definition: Drives acquisition, activation, retention and monetisation, often through CRM and lifecycle programmes.
strong: identifies the binding constraint in the funnel

competencies.name: Pipeline & prospecting
competencies.definition: Builds and manages a sales pipeline and converts it predictably.
strong: knows conversion rates and cycle times

competencies.name: Negotiation
competencies.definition: Prepares and conducts negotiations that create and capture value.

competencies.name: Key account management
competencies.definition: Grows and retains key customers through understanding their business.

competencies.name: Territory & distribution management
competencies.definition: Manages a territory, distributors and channel partners to hit volume, reach and profitability targets.

competencies.name: Product sense
competencies.definition: Understands users and problems deeply and designs products that solve them.
strong: starts from a specific user problem
competencies.structure: User -> problem -> solution -> trade-offs -> success metric.

competencies.name: Product prioritisation
competencies.definition: Decides what to build next based on impact, effort, strategy and evidence.

competencies.name: Product metrics
competencies.definition: Defines success metrics and diagnoses metric movements.

competencies.name: Product execution
competencies.definition: Takes products from idea to launch with engineering and design, managing scope and risk.

competencies.name: Case structuring
competencies.definition: Frames an ambiguous business problem into a tailored, hypothesis-led structure.

competencies.name: Synthesis & recommendation
competencies.definition: Pulls analysis into a clear recommendation with rationale, risks and next steps.
weak: summary of analysis without a decision

competencies.name: Estimation & market sizing
competencies.definition: Builds transparent, logical estimates with sensible assumptions.
strong: sanity checks with a second angle

competencies.name: Strategic thinking
competencies.definition: Thinks about long-term position, competitive dynamics and where to play / how to win.

competencies.name: Process improvement
competencies.definition: Finds and removes waste and variation in processes.

competencies.name: Supply chain planning
competencies.definition: Plans demand, supply and inventory across the chain.

competencies.name: Capacity & quality management
competencies.definition: Manages capacity, throughput and quality in operations.

competencies.name: Procurement & sourcing
competencies.definition: Sources goods and services for total value, managing suppliers and risk.

competencies.name: Talent acquisition
competencies.definition: Attracts, assesses and hires the right people efficiently and fairly.

competencies.name: Employee relations
competencies.definition: Handles grievances, discipline and workplace issues fairly and within policy and law.

competencies.name: People analytics
competencies.definition: Uses people data to inform decisions on attrition, engagement and performance.
strong: segments the data to find drivers

competencies.name: Compensation & benefits
competencies.definition: Designs pay and benefits that are competitive, fair and affordable.
strong: links design to behaviour and cost

competencies.name: Organisation development
competencies.definition: Improves organisation design, performance management, learning and change.
weak: training as the answer to everything

competencies.name: SQL & data manipulation
competencies.definition: Queries and transforms data correctly and efficiently.

competencies.name: Statistics & experimentation
competencies.definition: Applies statistics and experiment design correctly.
strong: correct interpretation of p-values and CIs

competencies.name: Data storytelling
competencies.definition: Turns analysis into clear, decision-oriented narratives and visuals.

competencies.name: Machine learning
competencies.definition: Builds, evaluates and deploys ML models appropriately.
strong: chooses metrics fitting the business cost

competencies.name: Data engineering
competencies.definition: Designs reliable data pipelines and storage.

competencies.name: CS fundamentals
competencies.definition: Data structures, algorithms, complexity, operating systems and networking basics.

competencies.name: Coding & problem solving
competencies.definition: Designs correct, efficient algorithms and reasons about edge cases (verbal walkthrough in this build).
strong: states approach and complexity before coding
competencies.structure: Clarify -> approach -> complexity -> edge cases -> test.

competencies.name: System design
competencies.definition: Designs scalable, reliable systems and APIs with explicit trade-offs.
competencies.structure: Requirements -> high level -> deep dive -> trade-offs.

competencies.name: Debugging & troubleshooting
competencies.definition: Diagnoses failures systematically in code and production.

competencies.name: Software quality & testing
competencies.definition: Writes maintainable code and tests at the right levels.

competencies.name: Cloud & DevOps
competencies.definition: Deploys and operates systems on cloud infrastructure reliably.

competencies.name: Security
competencies.definition: Understands threats, controls and secure design; responds to incidents.

competencies.name: Project planning & delivery
competencies.definition: Plans scope, schedule, resources and risks and delivers predictably.

competencies.name: Customer success
competencies.definition: Drives customer adoption, value realisation, renewal and expansion.

competencies.name: Legal analysis
competencies.definition: Identifies issues, applies law and contracts, and advises practically.

competencies.name: Regulatory compliance
competencies.definition: Understands and operationalises regulation relevant to the role.

competencies.name: Design process & craft
competencies.definition: Moves from research to concepts to tested designs with sound rationale.
strong: design decisions tied to user evidence

competencies.name: Research methodology
competencies.definition: Designs rigorous studies and interprets results with appropriate caution.

competencies.name: Clinical / life-sciences knowledge
competencies.definition: Domain knowledge for healthcare and pharma roles applied to realistic situations.

competencies.name: P&L ownership
competencies.definition: Manages revenue, cost and margin for a business unit with accountability for results.
strong: knows the levers and their size
